subs.desc: Scale-up vs scale-out trade-offs for databases and compute.

label: Relational Databases
desc: Production-grade RDBMS platforms used in data engineering stacks.

subs.label: MySQL
subs.desc: Open-source RDBMS — widely used for operational workloads and data sources.

subs.label: PostgreSQL
subs.desc: Advanced open-source DB with rich types, JSONB, and strong analytics support.

subs.label: MariaDB
subs.desc: MySQL-compatible fork with additional storage engines and features.

subs.label: Aurora DB
subs.desc: AWS-managed MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible DB with high availability.

subs.label: Oracle
subs.desc: Enterprise RDBMS common in large financial and operational systems.

subs.label: MS SQL Server
subs.desc: Microsoft's enterprise DB — often the source for CDC pipelines.

subs.label: Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD)
subs.desc: Type 1, 2, 3, and 6 — tracking historical changes in dimension tables.

subs.label: Star vs Snowflake Schema
subs.desc: Dimensional modelling strategies for data warehouses and OLAP cubes.

label: NoSQL Databases
desc: Non-relational databases — document, column, graph, and key-value stores.

subs.label: MongoDB
subs.desc: Document store — flexible JSON-like schema, widely used for semi-structured data.

subs.label: Cassandra
subs.desc: Wide-column store — high write throughput, tunable consistency, multi-region.

subs.label: Redis
subs.desc: In-memory key-value store — caching, pub/sub, session management.

subs.label: ElasticSearch
subs.desc: Full-text search and log analytics engine built on Lucene.

subs.label: Neo4j
subs.desc: Graph database — nodes, edges, Cypher query language.

subs.label: BigTable / HBase
subs.desc: Google's wide-column NoSQL — HBase is the open-source equivalent on HDFS.

subs.label: DynamoDB
subs.desc: AWS serverless key-value and document DB — millisecond latency at any scale.

subs.label: CosmosDB
subs.desc: Azure's globally distributed multi-model database service.

label: Data Warehouse
desc: Centralised analytical repositories optimised for read-heavy workloads.

subs.label: What is a Data Warehouse?
subs.desc: Purpose-built for analytics — column-oriented storage, MPP architecture.

subs.label: Data Warehousing Architectures
subs.desc: Inmon vs Kimball, lambda vs kappa, hub-and-spoke vs data mesh.

subs.label: Google BigQuery
subs.desc: Serverless, highly scalable cloud data warehouse — pay per query.

subs.label: Snowflake
subs.desc: Cloud-native DW with separation of storage and compute, multi-cloud.

subs.label: Amazon Redshift
subs.desc: AWS columnar data warehouse — RA3 nodes, Spectrum for S3 querying.

subs.label: Data Mart
subs.desc: Subject-oriented subset of a data warehouse — faster, focused analytics.

subs.label: Data Mesh
subs.desc: Decentralised, domain-oriented data ownership as a product.

subs.label: Data Fabric
subs.desc: Unified architecture connecting disparate data sources and consumers.

label: Data Lake
desc: Schema-on-read storage for raw data at any scale — structured, semi-structured, and unstructured.

subs.label: Databricks Delta Lake
subs.desc: Open table format adding ACID transactions and versioning to data lakes.

subs.label: Onehouse / Apache Hudi
subs.desc: Upserts and incremental processing on data lakes — Hudi table format.

subs.label: Metadata-first Architecture
subs.desc: Data catalogs, schema registries, and data discovery platforms.

subs.label: Serverless Options
subs.desc: AWS Lake Formation, Athena, Glue — fully managed lake infrastructure.

label: Cloud Computing
desc: The platforms and services that power modern data infrastructure.

subs.label: Cloud Architectures
subs.desc: Multi-cloud, hybrid cloud, landing zones, and well-architected frameworks.

subs.label: AWS (EC2, S3, RDS)
subs.desc: Compute, object storage, and managed databases on Amazon Web Services.

subs.label: Azure (VMs, Blob, SQL DB)
subs.desc: Microsoft Azure equivalents — Virtual Machines, Blob Storage, Azure SQL.

subs.label: GCP (Compute, GCS, Cloud SQL)
subs.desc: Google Cloud — Compute Engine, Cloud Storage, Cloud SQL, Dataflow.

subs.desc: Combining batch and streaming — lambda architecture patterns.

subs.desc: Open-source workflow orchestration — DAGs, operators, sensors, hooks.

desc: Distributed compute concepts and tools for processing data at scale.

subs.desc: Coordinating multiple nodes to process data in parallel.

subs.label: HDFS

subs.label: Apache Hadoop YARN

subs.label: Cluster Management Tools
subs.desc: YARN, Kubernetes-native Spark, EMR, Dataproc.

label: Big Data Tools
desc: The core processing engines for large-scale data workloads.

subs.label: Apache Spark
subs.desc: Unified analytics engine — RDDs, DataFrames, Spark SQL, Structured Streaming.

subs.label: MapReduce
subs.desc: The original batch processing paradigm — map, shuffle, reduce.

subs.label: Google Dataflow
subs.desc: Managed Apache Beam service — unified batch and stream processing on GCP.

subs.label: Kubernetes

subs.label: GKE / AWS EKS
subs.desc: Managed Kubernetes on Google Cloud and AWS.

subs.label: ArgoCD
subs.desc: GitOps continuous delivery for Kubernetes workloads.

label: Monitoring
desc: Observing the health, performance, and correctness of data systems.

subs.label: Prometheus
subs.desc: Metrics collection and alerting — time-series DB, PromQL, Alertmanager.

subs.label: Datadog
subs.desc: Cloud monitoring platform — APM, logs, dashboards, anomaly detection.

subs.label: Sentry
subs.desc: Error tracking and performance monitoring for applications and pipelines.

subs.label: New Relic
subs.desc: Full-stack observability platform — distributed tracing, infra monitoring.

subs.desc: Testing individual functions and transformations in isolation.

subs.desc: Great Expectations, dbt tests, schema validation — assertions on data.
